official.deadline_note: The MSc application, the scholarship application form, the reference letter and the English certificate must all be uploaded together before the scholarship deadline. TU Delft warns that missing the scholarship deadline means the scholarship application will not be reviewed. Award notifications are sent by email by the end of March 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 round with a 1 December 2026 deadline and decisions by end of March 2027; the scholarship application form on file is for 2027-2029
official.status_note: TU Delft lists the Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship with a deadline of 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET), two awards per faculty, within 16 full scholarships offered for regular MSc programmes; students are informed by email by the end of March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "Awarded students will receive full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme based on the Statutory or Institutional rate, according to the registered nationality, AND contribution for the living expenses." For the first year the coverage is stated as full tuition fees based on the statutory fee or institutional rate according to registered nationality.
benefits: Full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme, based on the statutory or institutional rate according to the registered nationality
Second-year allowances conditional on completing at least 48 of 60 ECTS by the end of the first academic year
Two scholarships per faculty, within the 16 full scholarships offered for regular MSc programmes
eligibility: You are an excellent international applicant, conditionally admitted to one of the 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes, but not to an International Joint Education Programme

Excellent academic results in previous study programmes relevant to the Master's you are applying for; as an indication you are amongst the top 10% of graduates, though proof of ranking is not required
You have submitted a complete MSc application before the scholarship deadline

A relevant bachelor's degree comparable to a Dutch research university bachelor's, with a CGPA of at least 75% of the scale maximum unless country-specific requirements apply, and the exact minimum met at the time of application
You meet one of the accepted English language certificates and scores, or are exempt (national of or bachelor's degree from Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the USA)
requirements: Complete your MSc application in the admission procedure before the scholarship deadline
Upload the Scholarship Application Form for 2027-2029
Upload one reference letter; if you have two references, upload them as a single PDF
Upload the English language certificate with your MSc application before the scholarship deadline, unless you are exempt
Holders may not receive any other partial or full scholarship funding in addition to this scholarship
documents: Completed MSc application, meeting the admission requirements of the chosen programme
Reference letter, or two combined into one PDF
English language certificate (IELTS, TOEFL iBT or Cambridge), with the TRF number, appointment number or verification number for verification
selection_criteria: Excellent academic results in previous study programmes relevant to the Master's programme applied for
Indicative ranking amongst the top 10% of graduates in the previous study programme, with proof of ranking not required
Comparison across the applicant pool, with two awards available per faculty
coverage: Full tuition fees for the first year for a TU Delft MSc programme, based on the statutory fee or institutional rate according to registered nationality
Second-year allowances only with sufficient study progress, namely at least 48 of 60 ECTS completed by the end of the first academic year
No coverage of travel, insurance or relocation costs is published
application_method: Complete your MSc application through the TU Delft admission procedure, checking the admission requirements for the programme
Upload the Scholarship Application Form together with your MSc application before 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET)
Upload one reference letter, combining two references into a single PDF
Upload your English language certificate with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline, unless exempt
Await the email notification of the outcome by the end of March 2027
official.application_route: Apply for the MSc through the normal TU Delft admission route and upload the scholarship application form, reference letter and English certificate as part of the same application before the 1 December 2026 deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time, 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programme
official.citizenship_residency: Open to excellent international applicants; the scholarship is not restricted to a nationality list, though tuition is charged at the statutory or institutional rate according to registered nationality
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to excellent international applicants to regular TU Delft MSc programmes
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes are eligible; International Joint Education Programmes are excluded. TU Delft also offers two partial Electrical Engineering Faculty scholarships, which are a separate scheme
official.duration: Two years, subject to satisfactory academic progress of at least 48 ECTS out of 60 in the first year; financial extensions beyond the 2-year period are not supported
official.description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen, who studied at TU Delft in the 1940s and believed technological developments would contribute to solving societal issues. Awarded students receive full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme based on the statutory or institutional rate according to registered nationality, plus a contribution for living expenses.
official.program_type: Excellence scholarship for incoming MSc students, funded by the Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence foundation
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 with at least 6.5 per section, or TOEFL iBT with overall 5 and 4.5 per section for certificates obtained after 21 January 2026 (overall 100 with 22 per section for earlier certificates), or Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency with an overall score of 185. The test must be no older than two years on the day you apply. Exempt if you are a national of Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the USA, or hold a bachelor's degree obtained in one of those countries.

applicant_utility.summary: This scholarship is won in the MSc application, not alongside it: the form, the reference letter and the English certificate all have to be inside your admission application by 1 December 2026, and TU Delft states outright that a missed scholarship deadline means the application is never reviewed. With only two awards per faculty, your odds depend heavily on which faculty you apply through, so the choice of programme is also a choice of competition level. Think of the top-10% guideline as a filter rather than a hurdle: no ranking proof is requested, but a borderline transcript in a competitive faculty will simply be outranked.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants in the top fraction of their cohort with a relevant, well-graded bachelor's degree and a strong supervisor reference, who can submit a complete MSc application by 1 December 2026 and can show real top-decile performance.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme is a 2-year regular MSc and not an International Joint Education Programme before investing in the application

Book the IELTS Academic or TOEFL iBT early enough that the score report and verification number are available before 1 December 2026, since the certificate must be no older than two years on the day you apply
Ask your referee for a letter that speaks to research aptitude and subject relevance, not just character, and merge two references into one PDF yourself
Check your CGPA against 75% of the scale maximum and any country-specific requirement, since the minimum must be met at the time of application with no rounding
Verify whether your nationality or degree exempts you from the English test before paying for a test
common_rejection_risks: Uploading scholarship documents after the MSc application is submitted, which breaks the requirement that everything is submitted together
Applying to an International Joint Education Programme, which is excluded from the scheme
Submitting two reference letters as separate files instead of one combined PDF
Assuming the English certificate can follow later, when the scholarship requires it with the MSc application before the deadline
A CGPA that is rounded up to meet 75%, when TU Delft states rounding is not accepted and later transcripts are not considered
Holding another partial or full scholarship, which is expressly not allowed alongside this award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel, insurance and relocation to Delft are not covered, and the living-expenses contribution is a contribution rather than a full subsistence allowance, so you should plan for flights, the Dutch residence permit process, health insurance and the normal cost of living in Delft alongside it.
document_audit: Two references must be merged into a single PDF, so agree the format with your referees early
TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted and all required scores must come from a single test sitting
IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted, so a single weak section can be retaken without resitting the whole test
You must supply a verification number for your English test, so keep the appointment or TRF number from the test day
Receiving the scholarship is conditional on fulfilling all admission criteria, so a late bachelor's degree or unmet condition voids the award
alerts: TU Delft states up front that scholarship demand far exceeds supply and advises applicants to check the tuition and finance pages before committing to a two-year programme
A bachelor's degree from an overseas branch campus of a UK, US, Canadian, Irish, Australian or New Zealand university does not give you the English exemption
Second-year funding requires 48 of 60 ECTS, so plan a first year that leaves room for that margin rather than loading it with risky electives
Part-time work alongside the scholarship is discouraged by TU Delft because it may affect your studies
Programme-specific criteria sit on top of the general requirements, so check the MSc programme page in addition to the general admission requirements
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One combined submission through the MSc admission route: the admission application, the scholarship form, the merged reference letter and the English certificate all go in before 1 December 2026, then faculty review and an email decision by the end of March 2027.
